chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Panassie's Quintet of the Hot Club of France
summary: Panassie heard their Sunday set and soon announced his own Hot Club quintet; Delaunay and Cullaz claimed the credit on television and Grappelli declined to appear.

bands.name: Quintette du Hot Club de France

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And it was just like -- we would work like -- it was more like brotherhood than anything else between us. We would go from one to another; when we'd finish we'd go down to his place, but Panassie, he saw a good thing in the quintet, and he came one -- we had a special -- we made a special tea-dance on Sundays to get the youngsters, you see, and

he came up one Sunday afternoon, and he saw the band together, and we really had the quintet just play for themselves, you see, and he had probably gotten the idea, -- a couple of weeks after we saw in the Jazz Hot, in the Jazz -- that Panassie had formed and organized the Hot Club, the Quintet de France.
And that guy, Maurice Cullaz -- you know him?

He seconded -- Charles Delauney and Maurice Cullaz, and then they invented the same thing, that they had organized the Hot Club, and it was televised -- on the television. I'm sitting here, listening to them.
And they -- on the program, Grapelly was supposed to be present. He didn't show
up. I said to myself, 'Thanks,' and Grapelly understood, and he didn't show up.
I saw Grapelly afterwards, and he said, 'Oui, je amad aux sujet de cet homme.' 'Someone told me about the television set-up,' he said, 'And I didn't intend to go,' he said.
Because he said, 'you know it wasn't true.'
